nodes.html: We are a hockey family. Our weekends are usually defined by early mornings, cold rinks, and long drives to games. But lately, those drives have felt heavy. The things we see out the window have changed, and naturally, so has the conversation in the car.

any.message: Element has sufficient color contrast of 11.28

nodes.html: Like everyone else in the Twin Cities, we were watching the news. We saw the images of the occupation. We were heartbroken by the murder of Renée Good. But for my wife Annie and our daughters, Aria (12) and Ellie (10), it wasn’t just something on a screen.

nodes.html: The breaking point for us happened on I-94. We were driving into Minneapolis for another tournament game, passing under the bridges that cross the highway. We looked up and saw crowds of protesters standing in the cold, holding signs, demanding justice and chanting “ICE OUT!”

nodes.html: It was quiet in the car for a moment, and then Ellie said something to us that I won’t forget:

nodes.html: “I want to go and protest.”

nodes.html: That was the moment we realized we couldn’t just drive past it anymore. We started small—buying groceries and supplies for families in need—but then I felt the itch to do something more.
